newsitem.title: UK: Laird group slips after profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Laird group slips after profits fall.

text.p: Shares in Laird Group Plc fell on Friday after the engineering group reported a drop in pre-tax profits in the first six months of the year.

The company, which makes automotive and industrial parts, reported an 11 percent decline in pre-tax profits to 33.4 million stg and said the year had started slowly after an exceptionally strong 1995.
Most of the shortfall occurred in the first quarter, it said.
The shares slipped back 29p -- a fall of nearly six percent -- to 457-1/2p in early trading.
"The headline figure is disappointing though they had warned on a number of occasions that the first half wouldn't be as good as last year's," said SG Strauss Turnbull analyst Zafar Khan.
Falls in sealing system profits and comments on pricing pressure were also disappointing, he said.

Profits in the Sealing System division fell to 12.8 million stg from 16.2 million stg. Laird said the car body seal plants in Germany were being affected by lower volumes and customer demands for lower price products.
The complete lack of any sort of outlook was also creating some uncertainty ahead of the results meeting, analysts said.
